rationale: The small espresso crossover gives individual fatigue differences in both directions and uses brewed coffee in both arms. Observational caffeine histories do not isolate coffee. One caffeine-capsule trial gives an imprecise FSS estimate. The later Café-PD study lists fatigue but its main paper reports daytime sleepiness separately and the fatigue result remains unverified.

The ground-pepper add-on to turmeric gave an inconclusive chronic-pain comparison. Topical and inhaled comparisons use different preparations. A metabolic pilot reported back pain and headache while using five extracts, without symptom counts or ingredient attribution. The cracked-pepper effect in Parkinson pain remains unresolved.

A six-week clinical crossover outside Parkinson disease favored freeze-dried whole blueberry powder on constipation severity by 0.3 points, with its confidence interval reaching zero after rounding. A separate feasibility trial reported one constipation event around six weeks in the powder arm, judged possibly related. These exposures and populations weakly inform a raw-blueberry improvement hypothesis.

Quebec motor studies used apple cutting and eating as one performance task. They assessed resting tremor separately and pooled some participant data across reports. The shared vegetarian menu and the apple-puree lunch also do not isolate a measured change after eating raw apple. Worsening and improvement remain unresolved.
